intro: Walk into a Buddhist temple and you may see shelves of books, bundles of palm leaves or long scrolls. These are Buddhist scriptures. There are so many that people call them a library, not one book.

In this unit you will learn how the oldest collection, the Tipitaka, is sorted into three baskets. You will see where the Dhammapada and the Jatakas fit. You will also learn about the Mahayana sutras kept in Chinese and Tibetan.

Then you will follow the teachings on their long trip. They went from memory and chanting to palm leaves, printed scrolls and English books. By the end, you will be able to explain how the Buddhist library is built and how it traveled.
bigQuestion: What are the Buddhist scriptures, and how did they reach us?

timeline.t: The Buddha teaches in northern India (dates vary; many scholars say the 5th century BCE).
Tradition says the First Council meets at Rajagaha soon after the Buddha's death (dates vary).
In King Ashoka's time, Buddhism reaches Sri Lanka.
Tradition says monks write the Pali Canon on palm leaves at Aluvihara.
Buddhist texts begin to reach China.
Kumarajiva translates many sutras into Chinese.
Tibetan scholars begin large translation projects.
The Diamond Sutra is block printed in China.
Muller's Dhammapada appears; Rhys Davids founds the Pali Text Society.
Buddhist speakers address the World's Parliament of Religions in Chicago.
The Dunhuang library cave is found in China.
The Buddhist Temple of Chicago is founded.

words.d: "three baskets"; the collection of scriptures in the Pali language
an old language of India used for Theravada Buddhist scriptures
the basket of rules for Buddhist monks and nuns
a talk or teaching of the Buddha (Sanskrit: sutra)
the basket of careful lists and explanations about the mind
a book of 423 short verses in the Pali Canon
a story of one of the Buddha's earlier lives
"great vehicle"; the branch of Buddhism common in East Asia and Tibet
a meeting to decide something important
teachings passed on by speaking and memory, not writing
a text turned from one language into another

test.q: Which basket holds rules for monks and nuns?
test.why: The Vinaya holds the monastic rules.

test.q: Which basket holds the Buddha's talks?
test.why: The Sutta basket holds the talks.

choices: in the Khuddaka Nikaya of the Sutta basket
test.why: The Dhammapada is one of the shorter books of the Khuddaka Nikaya.

test.q: How many verses does the Dhammapada have?
test.why: It has 423 verses. 547 is about the number of Jatakas.

choices: stories of the Buddha's earlier lives
test.why: Buddhists tell the Jatakas as the Buddha's earlier lives.
The Heart Sutra is Mahayana. The others are in the Pali Canon.
Suttas open with evam me sutam, "Thus have I heard."

test.q: Who does tradition say recited the suttas at the First Council?
test.why: Tradition says Ananda recited the suttas.

test.q: How were the teachings kept for centuries?
test.why: The teachings were kept by oral tradition.

test.q: Where does tradition say the Pali Canon was first written?
test.why: The Sri Lankan chronicles name Aluvihara.

test.q: What is the oldest dated printed book known?
test.why: The Dunhuang Diamond Sutra is dated 868 CE.

test.q: Who translated many sutras into Chinese around 400 CE?
test.why: Kumarajiva was a famous translator into Chinese.

test.q: Why do people say Buddhism has no single Bible?
test.why: Theravada, Mahayana and Vajrayana Buddhists treasure different collections.

test.q: Who spoke for Buddhism in Chicago in 1893?
test.why: Dharmapala and Soyen Shaku spoke at the World's Parliament of Religions.

write.prompt: How did the Buddha's teachings reach us? Explain in a paragraph. Name at least two texts or events from the unit, such as the First Council (Vinaya, Cullavagga 11), Dhammapada 5 (tr. Muller, 1881) or the Diamond Sutra of 868 CE.
tips: Name each text or event you use.
Say "tradition says" or "scholars say" when you give a story or date.
Put events in order: memory, palm leaves, printing, translation.
Use unit words like oral tradition, manuscript and translation.
